title: Geometric Control of Cat States in High Harmonic Generation
authors: Arti Gaharwar, Rocío Borrego-Varillas, Marcelo F. Ciappina, Anna G. Ciriolo, Javier Rivera-Dean, Philipp Stammer, Paraskevas Tzallas, Emilio Pisanty, Maciej Lewenstein
abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) provides a powerful platform for exploring the interaction between intense laser fields and matter on ultrafast timescales. Beyond its conventional description in terms of emitted radiation and electron dynamics, a fully quantum treatment of HHG reveals that the nonlinear light-matter interaction can modify the quantum state of the driving field itself, establishing correlations between the fundamental and harmonic modes. This perspective opens new possibilities for using HHG as a tool to engineer and control nonclassical states of light. In this work, we investigate the geometric properties of optical Schroedinger cat states generated in HHG via conditioning and post-selection. By analyzing the coherent-state displacements induced by different structured driving fields, we characterize the resulting phase-space evolution and the associated geometric phases of the generated quantum states. Particular emphasis is placed on how the polarization and spatial-mode structure of the driving light influence the geometry and evolution of displaced coherent states. Our results demonstrate that structured light offers a versatile means of controlling the geometric dynamics of HHG-generated cat states across the parameter space. Furthermore, we discuss the prospects for realizing genuinely topological optical cat states by exploiting more complex structured light configurations.
summary: This research explores how the geometric properties of optical Schrödinger cat states can be controlled by manipulating the structured light fields used in High Harmonic Generation (HHG). By analyzing the phase-space evolution, the authors demonstrate that structured light provides a powerful tool to steer and control the geometric dynamics of these nonclassical states. This opens avenues for realizing complex, potentially topological, quantum states of light.
main_problem: The paper investigates the geometric and topological properties of optical Schrödinger cat states generated through the High Harmonic Generation (HHG) process.
main_result: Structured light fields, such as those with rotating polarization ellipses or full Poincaré beams, offer a versatile means to control the geometric dynamics and associated geometric phases of these generated cat states.
method: The analysis involves treating HHG quantum mechanically, calculating the conditional state of the fundamental mode, and characterizing the geometric phase using the Berry connection derived from the structured driving fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is the interaction of intense laser fields with matter, modeled via the HHG process. The resulting quantum state is approximated as a superposition of coherent states (cat state) whose evolution is governed by the structured driving field parameters.
key_observables: Geometric phases, coherent-state displacements, and the harmonic yield spectra.
important_parameters: Polarization structure (ellipticity, orientation) and spatial-mode structure (e.g., vortex modes) of the driving light.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a simplified effective framework for the conditional state and uses the Strong-Field Approximation (SFA) for dipole moment calculations, neglecting macroscopic propagation effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structured driving fields (FRE and FPB) and show the resulting HHG spectra and the spatial distribution of harmonic intensity as a function of the control parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the quantum nature of HHG and the resulting cat state, to deriving the mathematical framework for geometric phase calculation using structured fields, and finally demonstrating control over these geometric properties using specific structured light configurations.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum optics, nonlinear light-matter interaction, and geometric phases, providing a concrete platform (HHG) to study the control of nonclassical light states using structured fields, which is highly relevant to quantum optics.
